read.passage: Last week, our school radio team interviewed Mr Salem, the head teacher, about the new reading corner. He told us that the corner would open after the mid-year holiday. He said that students had chosen most of the books themselves. When we asked him whether students could borrow the books, he said they could take two books home every week. However, he asked everyone to look after the books and return them on time. The team also spoke to Huda in Year 8. She said the reading corner was a great idea because the library was often too crowded. She admitted that she didn't read much before, but she wanted to take up reading this year.

qs.q: When will the reading corner open?
options: at the end of the year

read2.passage: Last month, our class visited the offices of a local newspaper in Dammam. The editor, Ms Rania, told us that a good reporter always checks facts with at least two people. She asked us what we would write about if we worked there, and most of us said sport. Then she gave us a challenge: we had one hour to interview someone in the building and write a short article. I interviewed the photographer, who told me he had taken more than a hundred thousand photos. Our articles weren't perfect, but Ms Rania said she was impressed and promised to print the best one next week. I can't wait to see if it's mine!

qs.q: What did the editor say a good reporter always does?
options: checks facts with at least two people
